chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Muhammad, from Al-Mu‘allā ibn Muhammad, from some of his companions, from Abū Baṣīr, who said:

I had a neighbor who followed the ruling authority, and he acquired wealth. He prepared singing-girls, and used to gather people to himself, and drink intoxicants, and he used to harm me. So I complained to him personally more than once, but he did not desist. Then when I pressed him, he said to me, “O you, I am a man afflicted, and you are a man kept safe. If you would present me to your Master, I would hope that Allah might save me through you.” So that entered my heart concerning him.

When I came to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام, I mentioned his condition to him. He said to me, “When you return to al-Kūfah, he will come to you, so say to him: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says to you: Leave what you are upon, and I guarantee for you before Allah Paradise.” So when I returned to al-Kūfah, he came to me among those who came. I kept him with me until my house was empty, then I said to him, “O you, I mentioned you to Abū ‘Abdillāh Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, and he said to me: When you return to al-Kūfah, he will come to you, so say to him: Ja‘far ibn Muhammad says to you: Leave what you are upon, and I guarantee for you before Allah Paradise.”

He said: So he wept, then said to me, “By Allah, Abū ‘Abdillāh really said this to you?” He said: So I swore to him that he had indeed said to me what I had related. So he said to me, “That is enough for you,” and went away. Then after some days, he sent for me and called me, and there he was behind his house naked. He said to me, “O Abū Baṣīr, no, by Allah, nothing remains in my house except that I have taken it out, and I am as you see.”

He said: So I went to our brothers and gathered for him what I clothed him with. Then only a few days passed before he sent to me saying, “I am ill, so come to me.” I continued going back and forth to him and treating him until death came upon him. I was sitting with him while he was giving up his soul, and he fell unconscious for a spell, then recovered and said to me, “O Abū Baṣīr, your Master has fulfilled for us.” Then he was taken, may the mercy of Allah be upon him.

Then when I performed hajj, I came to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام and sought permission to enter upon him. When I entered, he said to me first from inside the house, while one of my feet was in the courtyard and the other in the corridor of his house, “O Abū Baṣīr, we have indeed fulfilled for your companion.”

key_terms.السُّلْطَانَ: the ruling authority or political power
key_terms.الْجَنَّةَ: Paradise guaranteed by Allah for repentance
key_terms.الْمَوْتُ: death as it came upon him
key_terms.الْمُسْكِرَ: the intoxicant that he used to drink
key_terms.دَعْ: leave and abandon your present state

ai.seo_question: How does this hadith describe repentance through the guidance of Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This narration recounts the repentance of a sinful neighbor after receiving a message from Imam Ja‘far ibn Muhammad al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام promising Paradise if he abandoned his wrongdoing. It highlights sincere repentance, the transformative authority of the Imam عليه السلام, and the fulfillment of the promise at the moment of death.
